_past_papers/FEE2019_recollection.pdf.label: FEE 2019 candidate recollection (Part I & II, with handwritten Part II sheets)

part1.title: Cement type for seawater / coastal exposure
part1.explain: Slag (GGBS) or pozzolanic blends reduce permeability and bind chlorides/sulfates, improving durability in marine exposure. HAC loses strength by conversion; OPC alone is more vulnerable; quick-setting cement is irrelevant.

part1.title: Effect of increasing carbon content in steel
part1.explain: More carbon → more pearlite/hardenability → higher strength and hardness but lower ductility (and weldability).

part1.title: Truss member force by joints → elongation of a rod
part1.explain: Joint E: vertical of BE = 75 kN → $F_{\mathrm{BE}} = 75 \times 1.5/0.9 = 125\ \mathrm{kN}$ (T). Joint B: horizontal $F_{\mathrm{AB}} = 125 \times 1.2/1.5 = 100\ \mathrm{kN}$ (T). $\delta = NL/(AE) = 100 \times 10^3 \times 1200/(314.2 \times 200\,000) = 1.91\ \mathrm{mm}$.

part1.title: Load sharing in a bonded RC column (compatibility)
part1.explain: Equal strain: $\varepsilon = N/(E_c A_{\mathrm{c,net}} + E_s A_s) = 10^6/(25 \times 10^9 \times 0.067 + 200 \times 10^9 \times 0.003) = 4.40 \times 10^{-4}$ → $\sigma_s = E_s \varepsilon = 88\ \mathrm{MPa}$.

part1.title: Max BM in a beam carrying a secondary beam on rollers
part1.verify: Exact max is 1.125 kNm at 0.75 m from A (not exactly 1 kNm). Keyed (d) 'none of the above'; if the examiner only checked B, (c). Check against any official key.
part1.explain: Upper beam CD (2 m, 4 kN/m) puts 4 kN on AE at C and at the support. $\sum M_A$: $R(4) = 4 \times 0.5 + 4 \times 2 + 4 \times 4 + 5 \times 6 = 56$ → $R = 14\ \mathrm{kN}$, $R_A = 3\ \mathrm{kN}$. On AB: $M = 3x - 2x^2$ → max at $x = 0.75\ \mathrm{m}$: $M = 1.125\ \mathrm{kNm}$; $M_B = 1.0$, $M_C = 0$.

part1.title: Portal frame plastic collapse — beam, sway, combined
part1.explain: Beam (hinges B, load, C): $P \cdot L \cdot \theta = M(\theta + 1.5\theta + 0.5\theta)$ → 3M/L. Sway (A, B, C; D pinned): $P \cdot 1.5L\theta = 3M\theta$ → 2M/L. Combined (A, load, C): $P(1.5L + L)\theta = M(\theta + 1.5\theta + 1.5\theta)$ → $4M/2.5L = 1.6M/L$ ← minimum.

part1.title: Dry unit weight & saturation from sample mass/volume
part1.explain: $\gamma = 333\ \mathrm{g}/196\ \mathrm{cm^3} \times 9.81 = 16.67\ \mathrm{kN/m^3}$; $\gamma_d = \gamma/(1 + w) = 11.5\ \mathrm{kN/m^3}$; $e = G_s\gamma_w/\gamma_d - 1 = 1.262$; $S = wG_s/e = 94.5\,\%$.

part1.title: Which test gives total AND effective strength parameters
part1.explain: UCT/UU give total (undrained) only; CD gives effective only. A CU test with pore-pressure measurement gives both — not listed → (d).

part1.title: Bernoulli across a horizontal pipe reducer
Thrust on a circular gate in a 45° wall
part1.explain: Centroid depth $h_c = 0.5 + 0.5 \sin 45^\circ = 0.854\ \mathrm{m}$; $A = \pi/4\ \mathrm{m^2}$. $F = \rho gAh_c = 9810 \times 0.785 \times 0.854 = 6576\ \mathrm{N}$.

part1.title: Stepped bar: ratio of largest to smallest elongation
part1.explain: Equal lengths and force → $\delta \propto 1/d^2$. Ratio = $(35/15)^2 = 5.44$.

part1.title: Statical determinacy of three plane trusses
part1.explain: m + r vs 2j: (1) $5 + 3 = 8 = 2 \times 4$ determinate; (2) $9 + 4 = 13 > 12$ indeterminate (1°); (3) $9 + 3 = 12 = 2 \times 6$ determinate (stable).

part1.title: Static indeterminacy of four beams (supports, spring, hinge)
part1.verify: Candidate recollection highlighted (c) 1,4,5,2, but counting gives beam (4) = 1. Keyed (a); confirm the support symbols on the original figure.
part1.explain: Degree = r − 3 − (internal releases). (1) pin + 2 rollers: $4 - 3 = 1$. (2) fixed 3 + spring 1 + pin 2 + roller 1 = 7; 7 − 3 = 4. (3) 3 pins 6 + fixed 3 = 9; 9 − 3 − 1 hinge = 5. (4) pin 2 + roller 1 + spring 1 = 4; 4 − 3 = 1.

part1.title: Force carried by reinforcement in a short column
Effect of seawater as mixing water for OPC concrete
part1.explain: Chlorides slightly accelerate early hydration but reduce long-term strength and drive reinforcement corrosion/efflorescence → reduced strength (2) and durability (4).

part1.title: Location of max upward deflection, beam with overhang
part1.explain: By moments about B, $R_A = P$ acting downward. Between supports $M = -Px$, so $EI \cdot y = -Px^3/6 + C_1x$; $y(L) = 0$ → $C_1 = PL^2/6$. Slope zero where $x^2/2 = L^2/6$ → $x = L/\sqrt{3}$ from A.

part1.title: Effective stress below a river bed
part1.explain: River depth does not matter for $\sigma'$: $\sigma' = (\gamma_{\mathrm{sat}} - \gamma_w) z = (20 - 10) \times 3 = 30\ \mathrm{kPa}$ (30.6 with $\gamma_w = 9.81$).

part1.title: SI: unexpected soft clay at expected pile-toe stratum
part1.explain: Boreholes for piled foundations must prove competent founding stratum to an adequate depth below the toe — continue boring until competent material is proven (and extend the investigation).

part1.title: Gauge air pressure from an inclined water column
part1.explain: Water rises 2 m along a tube at 45° to the vertical → $\Delta h = 2\cos 45^\circ = 1.414\ \mathrm{m}$. $p = \rho g\Delta h = 9810 \times 1.414 = 13\,873\ \mathrm{N/m^2}$.

part1.title: Froude-scaled river model velocity
Stacked blocks, top block tied — min P to slide bottom block
part1.explain: Both interfaces resist: $\mu_s(100g) + \mu_s(250g) = 0.3 \times 981 + 0.3 \times 2452.5 = 294 + 736 = 1030\ \mathrm{N}$.

part1.title: Find n so max span moment is at L/3 from B (overhang load nw)
part1.explain: $R_B = wL/2 - nwL/18$. Max where shear = 0, at $R_B/w$ from B: $L/2 - nL/18 = L/3$ → $n = 3$.

part1.title: Velocity from a stagnation (pitot) tube rise of 1 m
part1.explain: $V = \sqrt{2g\Delta h} = \sqrt{2 \times 9.81 \times 1} = 4.43\ \mathrm{m/s}$.

part1.title: Rigid bar on two aluminium posts + shorter steel post (gap)
part1.explain: $k_{\mathrm{Al}} = 70\,000 \times 1250/250 = 350\ \mathrm{kN/mm}$ (×2); $k_{\mathrm{st}} = 210\,000 \times 1250/249.9 = 1050\ \mathrm{kN/mm}$. $700\delta + 1050(\delta - 0.1) = 500$ → $\delta = 0.346\ \mathrm{mm}$; steel $\delta = 0.246\ \mathrm{mm}$ → $\sigma_{\mathrm{st}} = 206\ \mathrm{MPa}$.

part1.title: Elastic-shortening loss when a pretensioned bar is released
Open-cut clay slope angle for $\mathrm{FoS} = 3$ (Taylor's chart)
part1.explain: $N_s = c_u/(F \gamma H) = 40/(3 \times 18 \times 3.7) = 0.20$ → read Taylor's chart for slope angle (candidate key: 65°).

part1.title: Ingredient that increases strength (water / air / SP / silica fume)
part1.explain: Silica fume: pozzolanic + micro-filler → denser ITZ, higher strength. Water and entrained air reduce strength; SP alone only enables lower w/c.

part1.title: BCA DfMA: rank manpower savings; CLT/glulam statements
part1.explain: BCA DfMA continuum (manpower savings at project level): precast ~10% < structural steel/advanced precast ~20% < mass engineered timber ~35 % < PPVC ~40%. CLT and glulam are both mass engineered timber; glulam is used mainly for beams/columns, CLT mainly for slabs/walls.

part1.title: In-situ test for undrained shear strength of clay
part1.explain: Field vane test measures $c_u$ of soft clay directly (SPT/CPT are correlations; pressuremeter gives modulus/limit pressure).

part1.title: Falling-head permeability test (0.9 → 0.5 m in 1 h)
part1.explain: $k = (aL/(At)) \ln(h_1/h_2)$; $a = \pi(0.003)^2/4$. Sample dimensions were not recalled — practise the formula.

part2.title: Strut–waler connection: web bearing & buckling of unstiffened waler web
approach: Web resistance to transverse force: EN 1993-1-5 §6 ($F_{\mathrm{Rd}} = f_{\mathrm{yw}} L_{\mathrm{eff}} t_w/\gamma_{\mathrm{M1}}$); type (c) load applied through one flange next to the diaphragm wall (or type (a) if through both flanges) — justify which.

$s_s$ from strut flange + 20 mm end plate with 45° dispersion; $k_F$, $F_{\mathrm{cr}} = 0.9 k_F E t_w^3/h_w$, $m_1$, $m_2$, $\ell_y$, $\bar{\lambda}_F$, $\chi_F$ → $L_{\mathrm{eff}} = \chi_F \ell_y$.
Compare $F_{\mathrm{Rd}}$ with 3500 kN; if inadequate: full-depth load-bearing stiffeners (EN 1993-1-5 §9.4 cruciform column check), concrete infill/packing between waler flanges, or a heavier waler.
Use UC 356×406×340 / ×235 section properties from the Blue Book (SCI P363); S355 with $f_y$ by flange thickness (EN 10025).

part2.title: Rectangular short column: N only, then N + M (design chart)
approach: 350 × 500, $f_{\mathrm{ck}} = 32$, $f_{\mathrm{yk}} = 500$, 30 mm cover to links. (a) $N_{\mathrm{Rd}} = 0.567f_{\mathrm{ck}} A_c + \sigma_s A_s$ with $\sigma_s \le E_s\varepsilon_{c2}$ → $A_s$; check $A_{\mathrm{s,min}} = \max(0.10N/f_{\mathrm{yd}},\ 0.002A_c)$ and $A_{\mathrm{s,max}}$ 4%.
(b) $d_2/h$ from cover + link + $\tfrac12$ bar; $N/(bhf_{\mathrm{ck}})$, $M/(bh^2f_{\mathrm{ck}})$ → EC2 chart → $A_s$; include $e_0 = \max(h/30,\ 20\ \mathrm{mm})$ check.
Sketch bars, links $\phi \ge \max(6,\ \phi_l/4)$, $s \le \min(20\phi_{\mathrm{l,min}},\ b,\ 400)$ ×0.6 near slabs (EC2 9.5.3). Justify bar sizes (spacing, buildability).

key_results.note: for the 3600 kN case: 0.567 × 32 × 175 000 = 3175 kN concrete

part2.title: Bored pile in clay ($\alpha$-method) + negative skin friction from fill
approach: Shaft: $Q_s = \sum\alpha c_u \pi d \Delta z$ ($\alpha \approx 0.5$ for bored piles in clay — state source, e.g. Tomlinson); $c_u = 30\ \mathrm{kPa}$ (0–5 m), $40 + 3(z - 5)$ (5–20 m).
Base: $Q_b = 9 c_{\mathrm{u,base}} A_b$ ($c_u = 85\ \mathrm{kPa}$ at 20 m). Subtract net pile self-weight ($\gamma_{\mathrm{pile}} - \gamma_{\mathrm{soil}}$) if asked for net capacity.
With $\alpha = 0.5$: shaft $188 + 1178 = 1366\ \mathrm{kN}$; base 385 kN; $Q_{\mathrm{ult}} \approx 1751\ \mathrm{kN}$.

(b) Fill consolidates clay → downdrag (NSF) above the neutral plane; reduces geotechnical capacity and adds structural load. Upper bound ≈ $\int\beta\sigma'_v \pi d\,dz$ or $\alpha c_u$ along consolidating length.

part2.title: Crest & sag vertical curves (SSD) + 3-layer AASHTO flexible pavement
approach: $\mathrm{SSD} = vt + v^2/(2g(f + G))$: 70 km/h, $t = 2.5\ \mathrm{s}$, $f = 0.30$. Crest uses $G = -3\,\%$ → 120.0 m; sag uses $G = -4\,\%$ (approaching from the other side) → 122.7 m.
Half-lengths $90 + 96 = 186\ \mathrm{m} > 150\ \mathrm{m}$ tangent → curves cannot be fully developed.

Pavement: $D_1 = \mathrm{SN}_1/a_1 = 2.3/0.45 = 5.1$ in; $D_2 = (\mathrm{SN}_2 - a_1D_1)/(a_2m_2) = 4.2$ in; $D_3 = (\mathrm{SN}_3 - \mathrm{SN}_2)/(a_3m_3) = 7.6$ in — round up to practical/minimum thicknesses and recompute.
Flexible vs rigid: lower initial cost, staged construction, easier repair/utility access, tolerant of differential settlement, smoother riding, faster opening.

part2.title: T-shaped column: N–M interaction diagram from strain compatibility
approach: Pure axial: $N = 0.567f_{\mathrm{ck}} A_{\mathrm{c,net}} + 0.87f_{\mathrm{yk}} \sum A_s$ (or $\sigma_s$ at $\varepsilon_{c2}$) with $f_{\mathrm{ck}} = 45$.
Pure bending: find neutral axis by force equilibrium ($\lambda = 0.8$, $\eta = 1.0$ for $f_{\mathrm{ck}} \le 50$), steel stresses from $\varepsilon_{\mathrm{cu}} = 0.0035$.
Balanced point: $x_{\mathrm{bal}}$ from $\varepsilon_{\mathrm{cu}}$ and $\varepsilon_{\mathrm{yd}} = 435/200\,000$; tension-failure point at $x = 100\ \mathrm{mm}$ as specified.
Take moments about the plastic centroid; plot (M, N) points and join.

part2.title: Sluice gate: specific energy, critical flow, hydraulic jump, bed slope
approach: $Q = VBy = 4 \times 2 \times 0.5 = 4\ \mathrm{m^3/s}$; $E_1 = y + V^2/2g = 1.316\ \mathrm{m}$.
$q = 2\ \mathrm{m^2/s}$ → $y_c = (q^2/g)^{1/3} = 0.742\ \mathrm{m}$, $E_c = 1.5y_c = 1.112\ \mathrm{m}$. $\mathrm{Fr}_1 = 1.81$ → supercritical.
Assume $y_2$ is uniform (normal) depth downstream: $S_0 = (nQ/(AR^{2/3}))^2 \approx 0.0035$.

part2.title: Primary clarifier sizing + sludge volume; activated sludge V, MLVSS, $\theta_c$
approach: SS removed = $0.75 \times 45\,000 \times 32\ \mathrm{g} = 1080\ \mathrm{kg/d}$; sludge mass = $1080/0.015 = 72\,000\ \mathrm{kg/d}$ → volume = $72\,000/1005 = 71.6\ \mathrm{m^3/d}$.
Combined $Q = 520\ \mathrm{m^3/d}$, $\mathrm{BOD} = 611.5\ \mathrm{mg/L}$ → 318 kg/d; $V = 318/4 = 79.5\ \mathrm{m^3}$; $\mathrm{HRT} = 3.67\ \mathrm{h}$.
MLVSS = $QS/(V \cdot F/M) = 6667\ \mathrm{mg/L}$. $\theta_c = VX/(Q_eX_e + Q_wX_r)$ with $Q_e = 425\ \mathrm{m^3/d}$, $X_r = 10\,000\ \mathrm{mg/L}$ → 0.55 d.

part2.title: Braced columns from a floor plan + sub-frame moment, slenderness
approach: Set in BS 8110 terms ($f_{\mathrm{cu}}$, $f_y = 460$) — legacy, not acceptable in FEE 2027. Re-do in EC2: $f_{\mathrm{ck}} = 28/35$ equivalent, $f_{\mathrm{yk}} = 500$.
EC2: $l_0 = 0.85 \times 4\ \mathrm{m}$; $\lambda = l_0/i$ vs $\lambda_{\mathrm{lim}} = 20ABC/\sqrt{n}$ (5.8.3.1); sub-frame moments for column B; nominal curvature if slender.

part2.title: Pile selection next to MRT viaduct; OCR of marine clay; NSF
approach: Bored vs driven RC piles: vibration/noise/heave next to MRT piles and bakau-piled shophouses favour bored piles (or jacked); address marine clay, groundwater, boulders.
Mitigation: monitoring (tiltmeters, settlement markers, vibration limits), casing, sequencing, LTA protection zone requirements.
Compare $p'_0$ with $p'_c$ → NC/under-consolidated clay → NSF acts; sketch axial load with neutral plane; toe into competent stratum (Old Alluvium/Jurong).

part2.title: Plate girder: classification, $M_{\mathrm{el}}/M_{\mathrm{pl}}/M_{\mathrm{c,Rd}}$, $V_{\mathrm{pl,Rd}}$, shear flow, weld
approach: EC3 Table 5.2 classification; $W_{\mathrm{el}}/W_{\mathrm{pl}}$ from built-up geometry; EN 1993-1-5 shear buckling if $h_w/t_w > 72\varepsilon/\eta$; shear flow VQ/I → fillet weld size (EC3-1-8 4.5.3.3).

part2.title: Fin plate connection
approach: SCI P358 (Green Book) checks: bolt group shear with eccentricity, bearing on plate/web, plate shear & block tearing, weld to supporting member.

part2.title: Prestressed RC beam
approach: Transfer & service stress limits, Magnel diagram, losses (elastic shortening, creep, shrinkage, relaxation).

part2.title: 400×400 column design + fire resistance with 4H25 ($\psi_{\mathrm{fi}} = 0.3$)
approach: Design $A_s$ for $N_{\mathrm{Ed}}$, $M_{\mathrm{Ed}}$ ($\gamma_G$ 1.35, $\gamma_Q$ 1.5), detail links $\phi8$ and cover 30.

Fire: EN 1992-1-2 §5.3 tabulated data (Method A): $\mu_{\mathrm{fi}} = N_{\mathrm{Ed,fi}}/N_{\mathrm{Rd}}$ with $\eta_{\mathrm{fi}}$ from $\psi_{\mathrm{fi}} = 0.3$; compare min b and axis distance a for R60/R90/R120.

part2.title: Bored pile DA1 design resistance ($\alpha$-method, $\xi$) + static load test
approach: $c_u$ linear 30 → 120 kPa over 30 m; $\alpha$-method shaft + $9c_u$ base; characteristic via $\xi = 1.55$ (model-pile procedure) → $R_{c,d}$ with $\gamma_s$, $\gamma_b$ for DA1-C2 (R4 set).
Working vs test (preliminary/ultimate) piles; characteristic from static tests: $R_{c,k} = \min(R_{\mathrm{mean}}/\xi_1,\ R_{\mathrm{min}}/\xi_2)$.

part2.title: 1.5 m pad on clay: influence depth, ULS DA1, consolidation settlement
approach: Influence depth where $\Delta \sigma_z \approx 0.1\text{–}0.2\sigma'_{v0}$ (2:1 or Boussinesq); if within Clay 1 only, no settlement from Clay 2.
ULS: undrained $(\pi + 2)c_u s_c i_c + q$ and/or drained Annex D for DA1-C1 & C2.
Settlement (NC, $\mathrm{OCR} = 1$): $s = \sum C_c H/(1 + e_0) \log(\sigma'_f/\sigma'_0)$ in sub-layers.

part2.title: Greenshields $v = 60 - 0.5k$; horizontal curve concepts; 2-layer AASHTO
approach: $v_f = 60\ \mathrm{km/h}$, $k_j = 120\ \mathrm{veh/km}$ → $q_{\mathrm{max}} = 1800\ \mathrm{veh/h}$ at $k = 60$, $v = 30\ \mathrm{km/h}$.
Speed-limit considerations: geometry/sight distance, crash history, roadside activity/access, 85th-percentile speed.
Horizontal curve: superelevation + side friction ($R = V^2/(127(e + f))$), transition/spiral curves, sight distance on inside of curve.

part2.title: 3 m rectangular channel ($S_0$ 0.002, n 0.015): $y_c$, $E_c$, $y_0$, jump
approach: Q not recalled — practise with the app's Manning calculator ($z = 0$). $y_c = (q^2/g)^{1/3}$, $E_c = 1.5y_c$; solve $y_0$ by Manning; compare $y_0$ vs $y_c$.
Jump with $y_2 = y_0$ (weir): $y_1 = (y_2/2)(\sqrt{1 + 8\mathrm{Fr}_2^2} - 1)$.

part2.title: Activated sludge
approach: F/M, V, HRT, MLVSS, $\theta_c$ — see PP2-clarifier-as for the formula set.
